event: A fire has burned at this spot for ninety-four days, and Fennick Rall has sat beside most of it.
He is sixty-three, and in three months he has not gone in.
He rises before dawn in the grey hour, wakes no one, and says nothing.
He picks up his pack, walks to the entrance, and goes in.
Three months before, his son Davin, a carter of twenty-six, went in without telling him.
Davin entered on the morning Fennick later reckoned as Death #4.
A man from the camp told him plainly fourteen days later; two days after, he started walking.
He arrived when the count stood at six deaths, and sat down by the fire.
He watched Sera Vant go in, then a scribe, then a man who studied the stone eleven minutes.
He watched a young woman roll a glass bead by his fire the night before she entered.
He spoke to none of them, and they did not need him to.
He watched the camp form round the dungeon like scar tissue round a wound.
He watched the ledger-keeper set up his table, and merchants come with rope and lanterns.
Four days ago a pale young man came back out and drew an arch on the blank cloth.
Under it he wrote: 300 meters in. Solid. Built by someone.
For ninety-four days he watched everything, and did not go in.
He steps through the entrance he has never been nearer than five meters to.
The warmth inside has a source; the ribbed corridor is no worse than mines he has known.
He carries a lantern and three days' food, packed correctly.
He reads the registry: Edric Voss, Maren Voss, Lira, Bren Aldic, Dara Hess, Mira Doss.
Then a gap, smooth and clean, and he stands before it a long time.
Past it, newer: Sera Vant, Sylas Renn on the keystone, Asha Trevane, first to arrive.
He cannot know whether the blank is Davin's; he touches it, and the dungeon does not respond.
Near the mouth of a side passage he picks up the warm amber-gold glass bead.
He knows the young woman meant to leave it, and sets it back where it was.
At three hundred meters he reaches the arch from the drawing.
Four meters, three voussoirs, unadorned: courage and craft in equal measure.
He reads the keystone, finds the lantern's oil half full and tended, and crosses.
The Ledger: Depth 2, the Warrens, Resolve +1, now 30.

changes.note: Depth transition into the Warrens, Resolve +1

event: The Asking finds him at the first junction, like someone calling his name in a crowd.
I want to find my son.
The Ledger names him The Witness, with the Gift Testimony: perfect replay of all he saw since camp.
Its Cost is Absence: while in Testimony he cannot perceive the present.
The Ledger reads Vitality 14, Resolve 29, Attunement 11, Fortune 16.
It notes him voluntary and non-Compelled: The Maw did not bring him here.
He stands a long time with that last line.
He sees he believed Davin was made to come, so the death was done to Davin, not by him.
He goes north, where the heat rises, as the accounts said.
He finds the scribe's journal against the left wall, sits by his lantern, and reads it.
He reads it as the record of five who died one by one, and the man who wrote them down.
The last entry: To whoever reads this.
He props it back at the same angle; the next person will need it more.
He uses Testimony for the first time, replaying Petra at camp describing the pattern room.
She went left at a junction and found walls covered in a fine script, repeated.
He goes left and finds the pattern room, its walls covered in Orvyn's cramped script.
He knows a man who wrote down his people's deaths because it was all he knew to do.
Recognition is not resolution, but it gives his ninety-four days a name.
He enters the Still Garden; the creature is at the far end of a row, plain to see.
The Ledger: Depth 3, Resolve +1, now 31.

changes.note: Depth transition into the Still Garden, Resolve +1

event: He notes a sword and a spear by the eastern wall, and no knife.
He and the creature watch each other, and neither moves.
After a while he begins to look for Davin.
He closes his eyes and replays the morning of Death #4.
He was never there, so Testimony gives only the shape of the missing memory.
He opens his eyes, his son's absence in his hands.
He lets himself see the crystals are beautiful: someone grew beauty in the dark.
The creature is no longer at the end of the row.
He had been told it moves when you are not watching, and he had closed his eyes.
He reaches for his pack, and the creature is simply there, and he is not.

changes.note: Fennick is killed by the Patient while in Testimony, Vitality to 0

event: The death report: Fennick Rall, the Witness, Depth 3, killed by the Patient in Testimony.
His Memory Crystal is bronze: patience, waiting without knowing if it will come.
No Floor Mutation; Witness complete.
The first non-Compelled voluntary entrant: The Maw did not bring him here.
The Ledger makes a new category: Voluntary Entrant, Non-Compelled.
His desire was real, and pointed at what the dungeon could not give him.
Davin is part of the dungeon as every death is, which is not the same as findable.
Testimony showed him the absence of his son, and that was truthful.
The Patient settles back among the crystals; four kills now, its name unchanged.
At camp the ledger-keeper writes: Fennick Rall, entered this morning, not returned.
In the margin: at camp about three months; knew the entrance better than most.
On the blank cloth Petra has written: Rall helped me read the pattern. Thanks, F.R.
The tally turns: 989 remain.
FENNICK RALL — DEPTH 3 — FIRST TO CHOOSE.
